acquisition: The peptides were subjected to nanoelectrospray ionization followed by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) in an LTQ Orbitrap XL
XCalibur software ver. 2.0.7 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, UK) was used for data acquisition.
labeling: Chromosomally normal- and Trisomy 21-amniocytes were quantitatively analyzed by using Stable Isotope Labeling of Amino acids in Cell culture and tandem mass spectrometry.
SILAC double measurements of Lys6 and Arg8
quantification: quantified based on MS/MS spectra ratios of peptides containing isotope-labeled amino acids
developing selected reaction monitoring (SRM) assays to quantitatively assess the differential expression

MStype_prompt.notes: The study uses a discovery phase with SILAC (DDA on LTQ Orbitrap) followed by a verification phase using SRM (Targeted). The primary large-scale data routing is based on the SILAC DDA workflow. No specific PTM enrichment (like phospho or ubiquitylome) was performed; N-terminal acetylation was listed as a variable modification for search parameters but not as a targeted enrichment assay.

cell_types: amniocytes (also known as amniotic fluid cells)
noncellular_sources: Amniotic fluid can be divided into two major components: supernatant fluid and free-floating fetal cells called amniocytes
scope: A total of 4919 unique proteins were identified from the supernatant and cell lysate proteome.
More specifically, 4548 unique proteins were identified from the lysate
Amniotic fluid cells were subjected to lysis using cold lysis buffer

ScopeCellTypeLine_prompt.notes: The study analyzed both the cell lysate and the supernatant (secretome) of cultured amniocytes. Since the primary focus and the bulk of the identified proteins (4548) came from the lysate, and the PRIDE accession specifically titles the project 'Amniocyte lysate proteome', whole cell lysate is the primary scope.

Treatment_prompt.reasoning: relative quantification of proteins produced from trisomy and euploid (chromosomally normal) amniocytes will reveal dysregulated molecular pathways
